perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- Ethan knows Gary is his long-time close friend from middle school; they have often supported each other.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he became concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. He told Gary that his health mattered, that he hated seeing him like this, and that the retreat might give him a new perspective.
- Ethan heard Gary initially refuse, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school, saying Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary later opened up to Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, then suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary; they discussed Gary’s progress and remaining challenges. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and continued offering support. Gary told him he was less overwhelmed and had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw that Gary seemed able to manage a healthier work-life balance on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him and decided to step back. He told Gary he was always just a call away and knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
